title.narrative: IRC - Conflict Prevention & Peacebuilding Programme in Somalia & DRC, 2017-2020
IRC - Konfliktförebyggande & fredsbyggande i Somalia & DRK

description.narrative:
International Rescue Committee (IRC) har ansökt om 38 000 000 SEK för att finansiera deras program "Conflict Prevention and Peacebuilding Programme in Somalia and Democratic Republic of Congo" som kommer att implementeras från 2018 till 2020. Programmets övergripande målsättning är att bidra till konfliktförebyggande och fredsbyggande i Somalia och DRK. För Somalia delen av programmet är målsättningen att förbättra tillgången till rättssystemet och stärka kapaciteten hos både lokala myndigheter och medborgare att förebygga och hantera konflikter eller tvister på ett icke våldsamt sätt. För DRK delen av programmet är målsättningen att bidra till att stärka lokalsamhällets motståndskraft och sociala sammanhållning genom att främja ett inkluderande deltagande av Twa- och Lubafolkgrupperna i de fredsbyggande och konfliktförebyggande processerna.
Till insatsen hör också en lärandekomponent för att dokumentera och fånga upp erfarenheter och kunskap till förmån för den bredare dialogen kring skärningspunkten humanitär verksamhet och fredsbyggande.
Bedömningspromemorian skrivs på engelska med anledning av att engelskspråkig personal i fält är delaktig i beredning och uppföljning av insatsen, i enlighet med Generaldirektörens beslut om Sidas språkvalsmatris med tillämpningsanvisningar från den 1 mars 2013.

International Rescue Committee (IRC) will implement the "Conflict Prevention and Peacebuilding Programme in Somalia and Democratic Republic of Congo" from 2018 to 2020. The programme is based on a Human Rights Based Approach and have the goal to strenthening access to justice and increase the capacities to prevent and manage conflicts (in Somalia) and to strenthening resilience, well-being and inclusive participation of conflict-affected Bantu and Twa through peacebuilding and conflict prevention initiatives (In DRC).

The objective of the project in the DRC is to contribute to peace and conflict prevention, as well as to strengthen resilience and social cohesion between the Twa and Bantu communities in the Tanganyika Province. The programme also helps to strengthen the local health system, so that more people have access to reliable and good quality healthcare.
The objective of the project in Somalia (in the districts of Hawl Wadag and Karan, Banaadir region) is to improve access to justice, increase knowledge of accountability, and strengthen the capacity of both local authorities and citizens to prevent and manage conflicts/disputes without violence.
The contribution also includes a learning component to document and capture experiences for knowledge and benefit for the broader dialogue around the triple-nexus (HUM-DEV-PEACE).

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
DRC project:
- The results of the final evaluation for DRC confirmed changing perceptions of inter-ethnic conflict, a key peacebuilding indicator. The percentage of Bantu community members surveyed perceiving that there is no conflict increased from 60% at baseline to 81% (women) and 80% (men) at endline. Among Twa respondents, the figures are 70% at baseline to 82% (women) and 79% (men), exceeding the targets set.
- Feedback collected through various exchanges with the communities, revealed e.g. that today, it is possible to sit on a bench and talk openly between the Bantu and Twa, that Many Twa have now settled in the villages and started to cultivate land, just like the Bantu, that women of both ethnicities wash at the same locations in the nearest river, and that children of both ethnicities play and attend school together. In other words, that the tensions that previously prevailed in the community have eased considerably.
- In relation to integration of gender, the partner worked with their local partner (who in turn worked through local structures) to incorporate gender mainstreaming into the project in different ways. For instance, the project supported women's participation and representation in different community structures and also added women' s literacy activities which encouraged and empowered women to take on roles in these community structures.
- Also, the rate of those confirming that they have access to local health services has increased from a baseline of 76% in 2018 (84% among Bantu, 66% among Twa), to 94% in total (97% among Bantu, 90% among Twa). The targeted health centres particularly saw an increase in the attendance of Twa women and for maternity care, compared to the baseline study.
- Furthermore, the volunteer community health workers (RECOs in French) have functioned as a social accountability mechanism - 29% of the community shared that they now speak directly to the RECOs and CODESAs (health center management committees), and village chiefs also received complaints from local community members. During the programme period, 46 health service complaints were identified, of which 44 were resolved and 2 were unresolved. The types of complaints were largely related to the quality of health centre services.
Somalia project:
- 73% of community members in the two districts who participated in the endline survey for the Somalia project confirmed increased trust and confidence in the formal justice systems which contributed to an increased number of people turning to district courts to solve disputes.
- 90% of endline evaluation participants reported that the project has built their capacity when solving conflict within the community and that they now have strategies to address conflict/violence at the district/ at village level.
- Related to gender aspects, it can be mentioned that the leadership of both districts, advocated through the project, for female police officers to be assigned to the district police stations to encourage women to report cases. One female police officer was then assigned to each district. Three women were also appointed to senior positions (Deputy DCs and Secretary General) in the Karaan district leadership. The project established and trained female peace committee members and paralegals that address issues of domestic violence and facilitate access to justice for women with provision of legal counselling. In addition, as a result of continuous advocacy, 13 females were recruited for local peace committees and 6 of the 10 paralegals were women.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
